newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina legislature okays Lumberton tax hike.
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina legislature okays Lumberton tax hike.

text.p: North Carolina's General Assembly has given final approval to a bill allowing City of Lumberton to double its motel room tax for three years.
The Senate voted 35-10 Monday night to accept House changes requiring that at least two-thirds of the new revenues be used for tourism-related purposes.
Because it's a local bill, it doesn't need the governor's signature.
The measure allows the city to increase the room tax to 6 percent from 3 percent through 2000 and is expected to raise $300,000 annually.
It creates Lumberton Tourism Development Authority to oversee expenditure of the portion earmarked for tourism. Carolina Civic Center will get the first $115,000 of that money.

The city will use the rest of the new money for police and fire protection and improvements on heavily traveled tourist routes. That will allow it to use revenues that would otherwise have been allocated for those purposes to build up its cash reserves.
